title: Ascending pathways to the brain
objective: Contrast the spinothalamic and dorsal-column pathways and where each crosses.

steps.title: Two roads up
steps.body:
Two main pathways carry somatosensation to the brain:

- **[[spinothalamic tract]]** — pain and temperature. It crosses the midline **in the spinal cord**, right near where it enters.
- **[[dorsal column–medial lemniscus]] (DCML)** — fine touch and proprioception. It crosses **in the brainstem**, higher up.

steps.prompt: Match each pathway to what it carries.
steps.explanation: Pain/temperature ride the spinothalamic tract; fine touch and body-position sense ride the DCML.

steps.setup: A spinal-cord lesion on one side cuts fibers that have already crossed for pain but not yet crossed for fine touch.
steps.prompt: What pattern of loss do you predict?
options: Pain/temp lost on the opposite side; fine touch lost on the same side below it
All sensation is lost on the same side of the body only, everywhere below the lesion
All sensation is lost on the opposite side of the body only
Pain/temp lost on the same side; fine touch lost on the opposite side below it
steps.reveal: Because the spinothalamic tract crosses low (in the cord) and the DCML crosses high (in the brainstem), a one-sided cord lesion gives *contralateral* pain/temp loss but *ipsilateral* fine-touch loss below it — the classic dissociated pattern.

variants.prompt: A one-sided cord lesion: pain/temp already crossed, fine touch not yet. The deficit pattern is…
options: Everything is lost on the opposite (contralateral) side
variants.explanation: Different crossing points produce the split: opposite-side pain/temp, same-side touch.

steps.prompt: Where does the spinothalamic (pain/temperature) tract cross the midline?
options: In the spinal cord, near where the fibers enter
In the brainstem, like the touch pathway
It never crosses the midline at all
Only once it reaches the cortex
steps.explanation: Pain/temperature fibers synapse and cross within a segment or two of entering the cord — which is exactly why their deficits appear on the opposite side of the body.

variants.setup: You need to recall where pain/temp crosses.
variants.reveal: It crosses in the cord, near entry — unlike the DCML, which crosses in the brainstem.

sources.note: Parallel ascending spinal pathways for affective touch and pain.

reviewNotes: Spinothalamic vs DCML, crossing points, dissociated loss.
